Profiles and posteriors of metafor fits

Source: R/adapter-metafor.R
metafor-methods.Rd

reliability_profile() of a random-effects fit of the metafor package gives the profile at its estimate of \(\tau^2\), a plug-in profile; reliability_posterior() of the same fit integrates over the between-study standard deviation instead, with the same estimates, sampling variances and moderators.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'rma.uni'
reliability_profile(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rma'
reliability_profile(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An rma.uni object, from metafor::rma() or metafor::rma.uni().

...

Must be empty.

Value

A reliability_profile object whose source names the method of the fit.

Details

The method reads the elements yi, vi, tau2, method and slab of the fit. With moderators, \(\tau^2\) is the residual heterogeneity, the variance of the true effects around the meta-regression, and the reliabilities are computed from it. In metafor's notation \(\tau^2\) is what this package writes \(\sigma_\tau^2\). A fit whose \(\tau^2\) is estimated as 0, as often happens with few studies, gives the limit of the profile at sigma_tau = 0 and a message; the posterior has no such boundary.

map_tau2_interval() maps the confidence interval of the fit through the diagnostics. Other fits of metafor, such as those of metafor::rma.mv() with several variance components, are refused with an error: the diagnostics need one between-study variance and known sampling variances. Fixed-, equal- and common-effect fits (method = "FE", "EE" or "CE") are also refused. Refit a random-effects model, or supply the estimates and sampling variances directly for a new analysis.

See also

map_tau2_interval(), and vignette("meta-analysis") for an example.

Examples

fit <- metafor::rma(yi = estimate, sei = se, slab = school, data = eight_schools)
reliability_profile(fit)
#> At `sigma_tau = 0` the profile is a limit: every reliability is 0.
#> ℹ The concentration count is its limit as sigma_tau goes to 0.
#> Reliability profile of 8 sites at sigma_tau = 0 (metafor REML estimate)
#> 
#>   informativeness I            0.000
#>   mean reliability             0.000
#>   dispersion H                 0.0000
#>   logit variance V             0.230
#>   concentration count J_eff    6.8 of 8 (limit as sigma_tau goes to 0)
#> 
#> At sigma_tau = 0 every reliability is 0.
reliability_posterior(fit)
#> Reliability profile of 8 sites (posterior)
#> Model: estimate ~ N(effect, se^2), effect ~ N(mean, sigma_tau^2),
#>        sites independent
#> Prior: flat on the mean and on sigma_tau
#> Summaries are conditional on the supplied standard errors.
#> Each site counts equally in the diagnostics, whatever its size.
#> 
#>                              mean     95% interval
#>   informativeness I          0.225    0.000    0.745
#>   mean reliability           0.230    0.000    0.735
#>   dispersion H               0.0143   0.0000   0.0283
#>   concentration count J_eff  7.2      6.8      7.9      of 8
#>   logit variance V           0.230    (fixed by the standard errors)
#>   sigma_tau                  6.58     0.243    20.8
#>   effect mean                7.93     -2.09    18.2
#> 
#>   Pr(I > 0.5)                0.138
#>   I at E(sigma_tau^2)        0.338
